scope: Thirtieth expansion batch: 12 mixed whole-predicate questions, four each for an earlier intention, an earlier completion belief and a current inference about a past action. Save/lock/pay/reserve occur in every class. Two plans are fulfilled and two are not; two completion beliefs receive later support and two are contradicted. This first final-plan batch does not claim to contrast every past hazu/tsumori formulation or to complete the separate normative mixed batch.

sources.publisher: The Japan Foundation, Nihongo Kyoiku Tsushin; Ichikawa Yasuko
sources.section: つもり（1）, sections1 and2: dictionary-form intentions versus ta-form beliefs/self-assessments; intention, schedule and decision are not identical. Section1(3) explicitly allows reporting third-person intention when known, rather than imposing a universal first-person rule. Section2 distinguishes the subject's belief from independently established truth and includes third-person belief reports. Some numbered examples were omitted by simplified extraction; only the visible prose and examples are used.

sources.publisher: The Japan Foundation, Nihongo Kyoiku Tsushin; Ichikawa Yasuko
sources.section: つもり（2）, sections1 and2: recalling an earlier intention with V-ru tsumori-datta versus an earlier completion belief with V-ta tsumori-datta. The actual examples illustrate interrupted intentions and mismatched self-assessments. The explanation locates the attitude in the past; these examples are not independent attestation of our fulfilled/confirmed original scenarios. Negation sections3/4 are not being retested or conflated here.

The Basics, Verb + tsumori, tsumori-datta and ta-tsumori sections. Plain-verb attachment distinguishes an intention from a belief in attainment. The study example introduces a belief in sufficient preparation before adding a later failure context. The failed-intention section and failed-test example illustrate common discourse uses, not universal outcome conditions. Categorical on-the-spot/third-person restrictions and global refusal-strength rankings are not adopted.

sources.publisher: The Japan Foundation, Nihongo Kyoiku Tsushin; Ichikawa Yasuko
sources.section: 「そうだ／ようだ／らしい」（1）, conversation3 and table2: you-da accepts plain predicates and can use indirect information rather than requiring direct visual observation. Its comparative attention/interest framework is not a fixed grading scale for the new cases.

sources.publisher: The Japan Foundation, Nihongo Kyoiku Tsushin; Ichikawa Yasuko
sources.section: 「そうだ／ようだ／らしい」（2）, information-based judgments, the actual past-event you-da example14, and the hazu/wake discussion. Supports inference from evidence and the existence of overlapping inferential resources. The broad subjective/objective ranking and 100-percent-certainty wording are not adopted; the passage does not quote or attest the original save/lock/pay/reserve sentences.

sources.publisher: Tae Kim's Guide to Learning Japanese
sources.section: Using hazu to describe an expectation: actual example1 yonda-hazu-da supports a current expectation about a completed event. Do not adopt the overbroad rule that all negative expectations must use hazu-ga/wa-nai, or the later categorical limitations on beki advice. Negative expectations and normative forms are outside this set.

sources.publisher: Tae Kim's Guide to Learning Japanese
sources.section: Using dearu for formal state-of-being and the complete conjugation chart: dearu/deatta are the affirmative nonpast/past forms; the text explicitly applies the regular past of aru. Use the noun-copula explanation and actual table, not the imprecise verb-or-adjective summary or an unrestricted requirement for wa in negative forms. Formality does not make the variants equally conversational.

Exact tsumori noun intention/plan and belief/assumption senses; the separate tsumori-de-aru entry includes a sure-that sense after a past-tense verb. These support lexical uses and the copular expression, not the naturalness or discourse neutrality of every invented past sentence. Spelling alternatives are not tested by this hiragana-only task.
Exact 保存/hozon entry, transitive suru verb; computing sense save to storage, not merely general conservation. Dictionary and ta forms are hozon-suru and hozon-shita.
Exact 掛ける/kakeru entry, transitive ichidan; the secure-a-lock sense explicitly cross-references 鍵を掛ける. Do not substitute its hanging, device-operation or other senses. The past is kaketa.

Exact 払う/harau entry, transitive godan-u; payment sense, not brushing away, effort or attention. The past is haratta, retaining the small tsu. Recognition of other spellings is not an equal-frequency claim, and this task requests hiragana.
Exact 予約/yoyaku entry, transitive suru verb; reservation/booking sense, not device programming or a contractual pledge. Dictionary and ta forms are yoyaku-suru and yoyaku-shita.

authoringNotes: All scenarios are original and require independent sentence-specific review. Pattern attestation does not establish every new collocation, and dictionary recognition does not establish contemporary frequency.

There are four lexical triplets and three functional targets, with the whole verb-plus-construction predicate missing. Every item has the same four-pattern instruction and a separate supplied dictionary verb; no item-specific form command supplies the answer. Full English remains visible and defines the requested message.

The named pool is V-ru tsumori-datta, V-ta tsumori-datta and V-ta hazu-da/you-da. Past copular deatta and nonpast dearu are also allowed. The32 accepted renderings comprise8 intentions,8 completion beliefs and16 current inferences. The two hazu and two you inference model buttons represent one shared functional target, not a forced hazu/you discrimination.

All answers include the supplied verb, in hiragana, and fit the entire literal blank within the80-character limit. The task excludes additional particles, contractions and auxiliary patterns. Other tense combinations, such as V-ta hazu-datta, and longer recollections with to-omotte-ita may be natural outside this named pool; they are not wrong buttons or globally condemned paraphrases.

The earlier saving and payment intentions are fulfilled, while locking and booking plans are not. The later check supports the earlier locking/booking beliefs but contradicts the saving/payment beliefs. These are scoped recollection scenarios, not a claim that every isolated tsumori-datta is neutral in tone or that its common discrepancy implication never matters.
The payment error concerns paying the wrong fee, not failing to do anything. The booking frames separate the time of the intention or belief, the time of booking and the room-use date.

Two current inferences concern the first-person speaker's own poorly remembered actions; two concern another person. This prevents first-person versus third-person subject choice from replacing the attitude/time distinction. Account records, a duty assignment and a receipt support judgments, not certainty about an operator's private thoughts or every procedural step.

The prior article and source records for plans, intention denial, past expectations and mixed completion/state were screened. Existing earlier-forward and qualified fulfilled-recollection hazu-datta practice is preserved, not relabeled as new coverage here. The separate normative mixed batch remains planned.

The Japanese scene may support another grammatical statement, but that is not necessarily the English message requested. In particular, a current inference may be true in a confirmed-belief scene without reproducing the earlier self-assessment. Accept all fitting in-pool realizations of the requested account rather than forcing the model wording.

All377 earlier parsed exercises, IDs and unrelated article passages remain unchanged. This content batch changes no runtime, schema, grading or SRS behavior. A separate preceding Android test-only change replaces the original one-set/eight-item assumption with a manifest-derived full-inventory comparison; it does not change import behavior.
